correctness.rationale: Writing x=sum d_v e_v+sum b_e a_e and y=sum h_v e_v+sum c_e a_e, the vertex equations are d_v h_v=0. Thus each vertex has exactly three types (0,L,R) with multiplicities 1,q-1,q-1. For an oriented arrow u->v, the xy arrow equation d_u c_e+b_e h_v=0 has rank zero exactly when d_u=h_v=0 and rank one otherwise, yielding W and the orientation-specific matrices WD or W^T D with each vertex weight inserted once; cyclic contraction gives the trace. For xy=yx=0, the two-arrow coefficient matrix has determinant h_v d_v-d_u h_u=0 by the vertex equations, and rank zero only when both endpoint types are zero. Hence each edge contributes q^2 if both endpoints are zero and q otherwise, giving tr(B^n) and the general graph subset sum. The displayed characteristic polynomials and C4 difference are algebraic identities; the bracket q^5+3q^4+8q^3-8q^2-q+1 is positive for q>=2 since q^2(q^3-8)>=0 and the remaining terms are positive. checker.py is finite corroboration only; the universal proof is the rank count and matrix algebra.
